lines.title: Hook
lines.text: Hey, I'm Taylor, and I'm a real person.

lines.title: Hook
lines.text: I'm also a user experience and product designer.

lines.title: Hook
lines.text: I'm going to show you something I've been working on.

lines.title: Hook
lines.text: It's called Color Taylor.

lines.title: Hook
lines.text: I'll just move myself out of the way.

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: You can find this demo the first time loading the app,

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: or from the question mark button at the top of the app.

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: Start with the sliders and controls you already know.

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: Moving one slider will highlight every other slider it affects.

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: Click the droplet button to switch between Source or Mixed colored sliders.

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: Click the tags button to show HTML colors on the hex.

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: Drag a handle on the hex and watch the RGB and HSB sliders follow.

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: Having fun is the goal of the tool.

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: It's a playground for people to interact with

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: and see the relationship between color models,

lines.title: Demo tour
lines.text: specifically RGB and HSB.

lines.title: The interface
lines.text: The color editor on the right should be familiar to most people who have worked with creative tools.

lines.title: The interface
lines.text: The hexagon on the left is a different way of displaying the same information.

lines.title: The interface
lines.text: The difference is that red... green... and blue each get their own direction on the hex, matching where they sit on the hue wheel.

lines.title: The interface
lines.text: Next, I'll show you what the different handles are doing.

lines.title: Hue
lines.text: Hue is an angle that ranges from 0 to 360 degrees.

lines.title: Hue
lines.text: The angle is cast from the center of the hex,

lines.title: Hue
lines.text: and its direction is based on the combination of red, green, and blue values for that color.

lines.title: Hue
lines.text: As you adjust the colors they dictate the hue angle.

lines.title: Saturation
lines.text: Raise the saturation and the three color values spread apart.

lines.title: Saturation
lines.text: Lower it and they flatten out.

lines.title: Saturation
lines.text: When all three are equal, there's no saturation, and you're left with gray.

lines.title: Saturation
lines.text: So saturation is the range between colors, from the highest value down to the lowest.

lines.title: Saturation
lines.text: Notice the hue didn't change. Same arrangement, only the distance between color values moved.

lines.title: Brightness
lines.text: Brightness is determined by the highest color value.

lines.title: Brightness
lines.text: At a hundred percent brightness the hex is at its largest,

lines.title: Brightness
lines.text: and lowering it shrinks the size of the hex.

lines.title: Brightness
lines.text: You can still reach full saturation at low brightness,

lines.title: Brightness
lines.text: it's just within a smaller range of RGB values.

lines.title: Bridge back to the editor
lines.text: Back on the editor side.

lines.title: Bridge back to the editor
lines.text: Remember the sliders lighting up in the demo? Here's why.

lines.title: Bridge back to the editor
lines.text: Saturation pushes the highest and lowest value sliders apart from each other,

lines.title: Bridge back to the editor
lines.text: or pulls them together when desaturating.

lines.title: Bridge back to the editor
lines.text: Brightness scales up the red, green, and blue values proportionally.

lines.title: Equations
lines.text: This app is meant to show the relations between colors as a playground,

lines.title: Equations
lines.text: but if you want the classroom perspective, check out the equations section.

lines.title: Equations
lines.text: If there's interest we can explore this more in the future.

lines.title: Figma plugin
lines.text: If you use Figma, I've also made a Color Taylor plugin that you might like to check out.

lines.title: Figma plugin
lines.text: You can access that from the top of the app,

lines.title: Figma plugin
lines.text: and I'll show you how the plugin works in a future video.

lines.title: Wrap
lines.text: HSL is in the app as well, but that's a video of its own.

lines.title: Wrap
lines.text: In the future I'd like to add OKLCH support.

lines.title: Wrap
lines.text: That's Color Taylor!

lines.title: Wrap
lines.text: Go play with it, and I hope it helps you see the relationship between RGB and HSB in a different light.

lines.title: Wrap
lines.text: If it's useful, I'd like to hear from you. Questions and feedback are welcome.

lines.title: Wrap
lines.text: Thanks, see ya.
